answers.why: Israel cries to God with the plural declaration that they know him.
Israel rejects good, and the following verse describes their appointing kings and making idols.
Israel is the source of Samaria's calf idol, which a craftsman made.
Israel is swallowed up and described in the plural as being among the nations.
Ephraim hires lovers as the people seek Assyria and alliances among the nations.
Ephraim multiplies sinful altars and treats God's law as foreign.
Israel builds temples after forgetting its Maker, alongside Judah's fortified cities.
Judah multiplies fortified cities whose palaces face destruction by fire.
Israel is addressed alongside other peoples and accused of unfaithfulness to its God.
Ephraim faces exile to Egypt, and the plural subjects eat unclean food in Assyria.
Israel will experience national punishment for its many sins amid destruction and displacement.
Ephraim is the community associated with the prophetic watchman and the surrounding collective corruption.
Israel is identified with the ancestral wilderness generation that went to Baalpeor.
Ephraim has plural possessors of glory and children whom God threatens to take away.
Ephraim is pictured as a planted community whose children face slaughter.
Ephraim brings its children to slaughter amid a collective threat of bereavement.
Ephraim's plural members lose their offspring and become wanderers among the nations.
